best_for: Developers and cloud admins who move files in and out of Azure blob containers, file shares and queues every week, and who would rather drag and drop than type `az storage` commands.

points.title: One window for Azure Storage
points.text: Browse, upload and download blobs, file shares, queues and tables, plus Data Lake Storage containers and managed disks. You can also set access tiers, permissions and access control lists without opening the Azure portal.

points.title: Many ways to connect
points.text: Sign in with an Azure account to see whole subscriptions, or attach a single resource with an account key, a SAS connection string or URL, or Microsoft Entra ID. National clouds and Azure Stack are supported too.

points.title: Works offline against Azurite
points.text: It connects to the Azurite emulator on Windows, macOS or Linux, so you can test storage code locally without paying for an account. It does not start the emulator for you; run it first.

points.title: Needs .NET 10 and 64-bit
points.text: Since version 1.42.0 the app needs a .NET 10 runtime that matches its architecture. The Windows installer adds one if it is missing, but keeping .NET updated is up to you. On Windows, only 10 and 11 are supported, and only 64-bit.

points.title: Linux: Snap is Microsoft's pick
points.text: Microsoft recommends the Snap Store package, which brings its dependencies and updates itself, or a .tar.gz where you install dependencies by hand. The Flatpak listed here is a Flathub build that Flathub does not mark as verified, and it sits at v1.47.0.

points.title: Versions kept on this site
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 52 versions, with x64 and Arm64 installers for either one user or the whole machine. macOS (Intel and Apple Silicon, macOS 12 or later) and Linux list only the current release, so downgrades there need another source.
